chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said:

I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: There belonged to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) a she-camel upon which he performed hajj twenty-two times, and he never struck her with a single blow at all.

He said: Then, after his death, she came, and we were not aware of her until one of our servants, or one of the mawālī, came to me and said: The she-camel has gone out and come to the grave of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, then knelt upon it, rubbing the grave with the front of her neck while she was moaning.
So I said: Catch her, catch her, and bring her to me before they come to know of her or see her. He said: And she had never seen the grave at all.

key_terms.بِجِرَانِهَا: with the front part of her neck/chest against the ground
key_terms.تَرْغُو: she was making the sound of a camel, moaning
key_terms.حَجَّةً: a pilgrimage journey; here, one of the twenty-two hajj journeys
key_terms.قَبْرَ: the grave of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام)
key_terms.قَرَعَهَا: he struck her; here, negated to show he never hit her
key_terms.مَوْتِهِ: his death, referring to Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام)
key_terms.نَاقَةٌ: a she-camel belonging to Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام)

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn’s she-camel in al-Kāfī relate about his character and the sign seen after his death?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) used a she-camel for twenty-two hajj journeys and never struck her. After his death, the animal came on its own to his grave, knelt there, and rubbed herself against it while moaning, which is presented as a remarkable sign connected to the Imam (عليه السلام).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There was a she-camel of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> performed Hajj upon it, twenty two Pilgrimages, not having whipped it with a whip at all.

So she came over after his<sup>asws</sup> passing away, and we were not aware of it except that one of our<sup>asws</sup> servants came over to me<sup>asws</sup>, or one of the slaves, so he said, ‘The she-camel came out and came over to the grave of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>. So she rubbed herself upon it by its side and she was moaning.
So I said, ‘Be aware of her, be aware of her, and go to her before they (people) come to know of her or see her’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And she had not seen the grave (beforehand) at all’.
en.sarwar: وَإِنَّ غُلاماً بَيْنَ كِسْرَى وَهَاشِمٍ***لاكْرَمُ مَنْ نِيطَتْ عَلَيْهِ التَّمَائِمُ‏ 1. al-Husayn ibn al-Hassan al-Hassani may grant him blessings and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah all of them from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abdallah al-Khuza’i from Nasr ibn Muzaham from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“When the daughter of Yazdjurd was brought to before ‘Umar the girls of Madina would love to see her. When entered the Mosque it become all delightful and bright. When ‘Umar looked at her she covered her face and said in her own language, “’Uff, bay ruj ba’ da Hurmuz (May, the life of Hurmuz turn black).” ‘Umar asked, “Is she abusing me and he turned to her. Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) said, “That is not for you. Give her the chance to chose whoever of the Muslims she likes and then count as his share of the booty. He allowed her to choose and she came all the way to placed her hand on the head of al-Husayn (a.s.). Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) asked her, “What is your name?” She said, “It is Jahan Shah.” Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) said, “In fact, it is Shahra Ba’nuwayh.” He then said to al-Husayn (a.s.), “O abu ‘Abdallah, she will give birth to a son for you who will be the best of the inhabitants of earth. She gave birth to Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.). Ali ibn al-Husayn was called the son of the two best. The chosen from Arabs was the tribe of Hashim and from none Arab was Persains. It is narrated that abu al-Aswad al-Du’ili said about it. “A boy from Kisra and Hashim the most noble one on who sacred symbols are stitched for safety.”
